This medicine can be administered by intramuscular or intravenous injection or by oral administration depending on the indication.

items.t: Antidote to coumarin anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin) in haemorrhage or threatened haemorrhage with low prothrombin or factor VII.

src.q: is indicated as an antidote to anticoagulant drugs of the coumarin type in the treatment of haemorrhage or threatened haemorrhage, associated with a low blood level of prothrombin or factor VII.

items.t: Prophylaxis and treatment of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) in neonates and infants; antidote to coumarin anticoagulants in infants and children on haematologist advice.

src.q: is indicated for the prophylaxis and treatment of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) in neonates and infants.
can be used, following specialist advice from a haematologist, as an antidote to anticoagulant drugs of the coumarin type in infants and children.

items.t: Children: consult a haematologist before using phytomenadione in any child (both products).

src.q: It is advisable that a haematologist is consulted about appropriate investigation and treatment in any child
It is advisable that a haematologist is consulted about appropriate investigation and treatment in any infant or child

items.t: Adolescents and adults needing coumarin reversal: use the 10 mg/ml product, not the paediatric product.

src.q: For use as an antidote to anticoagulant drugs of the coumarin type in adolescents and adults, refer to Konakion MM Ampoules 10 mg/ml

items.t: Severe or life-threatening haemorrhage on a coumarin: stop the anticoagulant; give 5-10 mg by slow IV injection (over at least 30 seconds) with prothrombin complex concentrate (FFP if PCC unavailable). Check INR after 3 hours; repeat if response inadequate. Maximum 40 mg IV in 24 hours.

src.q: The coumarin anticoagulant should be withdrawn and an intravenous injection of Konakion MM/Phytomenadione 10 mg/1 ml given slowly (over at least 30 seconds) at a dose of 5-10 mg together with prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC).
The patient's INR should be estimated three hours later
Not more than 40 mg of Konakion MM/Phytomenadione 10 mg/1 ml should be given intravenously in 24 hours.

items.t: Warfarin, major bleeding: 5.0 mg IV plus PCC; life-threatening bleeding: 5.0 to 10.0 mg IV plus PCC.

src.q: Warfarin Major bleeding 5.0 mg PCC1 Life-threatening bleeding 5.0 to 10.0 mg PCC1

items.t: Warfarin, asymptomatic high INR with or without mild bleeding: INR 5-9 give 0.5 to 1.0 mg IV; INR >9 give 1.0 mg IV (guidance only).

src.q: Warfarin 5-9 0.5 to 1.0 mg >9 1.0 mg

items.t: Reversal before surgery that can wait 6-12 hours: 5 mg IV; if surgery cannot wait, add PCC and check INR before surgery.

src.q: Patients who require emergency surgery that can be delayed for 6-12 hours can be given 5 mg intravenous vitamin K1 to reverse the anticoagulant effect.

items.t: Elderly: more sensitive to reversal; use the lower end of dose ranges.

src.q: The dosage for this patient group should therefore be at the lower end of the ranges recommended.

items.t: Warfarin SmPC (oral option): INR >8.0 with no or minor bleeding - 0.5-1 mg slow IV or 5 mg by mouth (smaller oral doses 0.5-2.5 mg using the IV preparation for partial reversal); repeat if INR still too high after 24 hours. SPS notes oral use of the IV formulation is off-label.

src.q: give phytomenadione (vitamin K1) 0·5-1 mg for adults, 0·015-0·030 mg/kg (15-30 micrograms/kg) for children by slow intravenous injection or 5 mg by mouth
either orally (off-label use of intravenous formulation) or intravenously depending on presence of bleeding

items.t: VKDB prophylaxis, healthy neonates 36 weeks gestation and older: either 1 mg IM at or soon after birth, or 2 mg orally at or soon after birth, then 2 mg at 4-7 days and 2 mg at 1 month (third oral dose can be omitted if exclusively formula fed).

src.q: Healthy neonates of 36 weeks gestation and older: Either: - 1 mg administered by intramuscular injection at birth or soon after birth or - 2 mg orally at birth or soon after birth.
The oral dose should be followed by a further dose of 2 mg at 4-7 days of age. A further 2 mg oral dose should be given at 1 month after birth.

items.t: Preterm under 36 weeks weighing 2.5 kg or more, and term neonates at special risk: 1 mg IM or IV at or soon after birth; further doses by coagulation status.

src.q: 1 mg IM or IV at birth or soon after birth. The amount and frequency of further doses should be based on coagulation status.

items.t: Preterm under 36 weeks weighing less than 2.5 kg: 0.4 mg/kg (0.04 ml/kg) IM or IV at or soon after birth; do not exceed this parenteral dose. Take care: 10-fold dosing errors are common.

src.q: 0.4 mg/kg (equivalent to 0.04 ml/kg) IM or IV at birth or soon after birth. This parenteral dose should not be exceeded.
care is required when calculating and measuring the dose in relation to the baby's weight (10 times dosing errors are common)

items.t: Treatment of VKDB: initially 1 mg IV, further doses by clinical picture and coagulation status.

src.q: Initially 1 mg IV and further doses as required, depending on clinical picture and coagulation status.

items.t: Warfarin reversal in infants/children (IV only, haematologist advice): partial reversal 30 micrograms/kg IV (the paediatric product suits this dose only in children over 13 kg); complete reversal of overdose 250-300 micrograms/kg IV (only in children over 1.6 kg). Check prothrombin time 2-6 hours later; repeat if needed.

src.q: the suggested dose for the partial reversal of anticoagulation is 30 micrograms/kg administered by IV injection
The suggested dose of vitamin K for patients requiring a complete reversal of a warfarin overdose is 250-300 micrograms/kg administered by IV injection.
is only suitable for the administration of doses of 30 micrograms/kg in children weighing over 13 kg
is only suitable for the administration of doses of 250-300 micrograms/kg in children weighing over 1.6 kg

items.t: Children 1-18 years (10 mg/ml product): major/life-threatening bleeding 5 mg IV (with PCC or FFP); asymptomatic high INR (>8) 30 micrograms/kg IV, recheck INR 2-6 hours later.

src.q: A dose of 5 mg vitamin K1 IV is suggested
Intravenous vitamin K1 at doses of 30 micrograms/kg have been reported to be effective in reversing asymptomatic high (>8) INR in clinically well children.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to any constituent.

src.q: Use in patients with a known hypersensitivity to any of the constituents.
Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: 10 mg/1 ml product must not be given intramuscularly (depot effect makes re-anticoagulation difficult; haematoma risk in anticoagulated patients).

src.q: This medicine should not be administered intramuscularly because the IM route exhibits depot characteristics

items.t: Severe liver impairment: each 1 ml ampoule contains 54.6 mg glycocholic acid (possible bilirubin displacement); monitor INR carefully.

src.q: Careful monitoring of the INR is necessary after administration of this medicine in patients with severely impaired liver function.

items.t: Mechanical heart valves: vitamin K1 is generally to be avoided unless there is major bleeding. Use fresh frozen plasma for transfusion in prosthetic valve patients.

src.q: The use of vitamin K1 in patients with mechanical heart valves is generally to be avoided, unless there is major bleeding.

items.t: Avoid large doses if anticoagulation is to continue (no experience above 40 mg per day). Vitamin K1 does not reverse heparin.

src.q: Large doses of Konakion MM/Phytomenadione 10 mg/1 ml (not more than 40 mg per day) should be avoided if it is intended to continue with anticoagulant therapy
Vitamin K1 is not an antidote to heparin.

items.t: Vitamin K may interfere with warfarin anticoagulation for 2-3 weeks; earliest effect at 4-6 hours, so severe bleeding may need clotting factor replacement.

src.q: vitamin K administration is likely to interfere with anticoagulation with warfarin for 2-3 weeks
the earliest effect seen with vitamin K treatment is at 4 to 6 hours

items.t: Premature babies under 2.5 kg: parenteral use may increase the risk of kernicterus.

src.q: Parenteral administration to premature babies weighing less than 2.5 kg may increase the risk for the development of kernicterus (bilirubin encephalopathy).

items.t: Infants with cholestatic disease must receive it IM or IV (oral absorption impaired). Coumarin reversal in children must be IV (IM may cause significant bleeding).

src.q: Infants with cholestatic disease must receive Konakion MM Paediatric/ Phytomenadione 2 mg/0.2 ml by intramuscular or intravenous injection since oral absorption is impaired in these patients.
must be administered by intravenous injection when used as an antidote to anticoagulant drugs of the coumarin type

items.t: Do not use if ampoule contents are turbid or separated.

src.q: In this case the ampoule must no longer be used.

items.t: Antagonises coumarin anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin); no other significant interactions known.

src.q: No significant interactions are known other than antagonism of coumarin anticoagulants.
No significant interactions are known other than antagonism of coumarin anticoagulants.

renal.note: No renal impairment advice in the phytomenadione SmPCs.

items.t: Severe liver impairment: careful INR monitoring needed (glycocholic acid content).

src.q: Careful monitoring of the INR is necessary after administration of this medicine in patients with severely impaired liver function.

items.t: Use in pregnancy only if benefits outweigh risks. Not recommended in pregnant women as prophylaxis of vitamin K deficiency bleeding in the newborn.

src.q: the administration during pregnancy should only occur if the benefits outweigh the risks
This medicine is not recommended for pregnant women as prophylaxis of vitamin K deficiency bleeding in the newborn.

items.t: Paediatric 2 mg/0.2 ml SmPC: vitamin K1 is poorly excreted in breast milk. No specific breastfeeding advice in the 10 mg/ml SmPC.

src.q: is poorly excreted in breast milk

reproductive.note: No fertility or contraception advice in the phytomenadione SmPCs.

adverseCommon.note: No common or very common adverse effects are listed in the phytomenadione SmPCs.

items.t: Anaphylactoid reactions after intravenous injection.

src.q: There have been reports of anaphylactoid reactions after intravenous injections of this medicine.

items.t: Very rarely venous irritation or phlebitis (IV). Paediatric product: rare severe injection site reactions (inflammation, atrophy, necrosis).

src.q: Very rarely, venous irritation or phlebitis has been reported
Rarely, injection site reactions may occur which may be severe, including inflammation, atrophy and necrosis.

items.t: Adults (major bleeding): INR 3 hours after dose; daily coagulation profiles until acceptable (more often in severe cases).

src.q: Coagulation profiles must be monitored on a daily basis until these have returned to acceptable levels

items.t: Children: measure INR/prothrombin time 2 to 6 hours after the dose; frequent monitoring of vitamin K dependent clotting factors.

src.q: Prothrombin time should be measured 2 to 6 hours later
Frequent monitoring of vitamin K dependent clotting factors is essential in these patients.

items.t: 10 mg/1 ml: IV only, slowly (over at least 30 seconds). For infusion in adults, dilute in 55 ml of 5% glucose, freshly prepared and protected from light; do not mix with other injectables (may inject into lower part of an infusion set).

src.q: should be diluted with 55 ml of 5% glucose before slowly infusing the product
should not be diluted or mixed with other injectables, but may be injected into the lower part of an infusion apparatus

items.t: Paediatric 2 mg/0.2 ml: IM, IV or oral. Use 0.5 ml syringes with 0.01 ml graduations for 0.04-0.1 ml doses. IV infusion not recommended (inject into lower part of a running infusion set). For oral use, draw 0.2 ml (2 mg) into the supplied dispenser and drop into the baby's mouth.

src.q: 0.5 ml syringes with 0.01 ml graduations are recommended
Administration of Konakion MM Paediatric/Phytomenadione 2 mg/0.2 ml by IV infusion is not recommended
Drop the contents of the dispenser directly into the baby's mouth by pressing the plunger.

items.t: Parents giving oral neonatal prophylaxis: complete the course of oral doses (birth, 4-7 days, 1 month unless exclusively formula fed).

src.q: In exclusively formula fed infants the third oral dose can be omitted.
